'''Adam John Morrison''' (born July 19, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Morrison played for three years at [[Gonzaga University]] and was considered to be one of the top [[college basketball]] players in 2005–06. He was a finalist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith]] and the [[Wooden Award]]. He was named [[Oscar Robertson Trophy|Co-Player of the Year]] with Duke's [[JJ Redick]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 31, 2006 |title=Redick, Morrison named co-players of year |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2390779 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> and won the 2006 Chevrolet Player of the Year award. He played for the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] from 2006 to 2009, and for the [[L.A. Lakers]] from 2009 to 2010, where he won two NBA championships.

==Early life==
Morrison's father, John, worked as a basketball coach, and the family moved with his coaching career: [[Casper College]] in [[Casper, Wyoming]], [[Dakota Wesleyan University]] in [[Mitchell, South Dakota]], and [[Dawson Community College]] in [[Glendive, Montana]]. When Morrison was in the fourth grade, his father left coaching,<ref name="bravehearts150">{{Cite book |last=Withers |first=Bud |title=BraveHearts: The Against-All-Odds Rise of Gonzaga Basketball |publisher=Triumph Books |year=2002 |isbn=1-57243-499-6 |location=Chicago |page=150}}</ref> and the family moved to [[Spokane, Washington]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-25 |title=Fans Barely Recognize Gonzaga Legend Adam Morrison Today |url=https://www.si.com/extra-mustard/2023/03/25/adam-morrison-fans-barely-recognize-gonzaga-legend-ncaa-tournament |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-26 |title=Gonzaga legend Adam Morrison headlines 2024 Hooptown Hall of Fame class |url=https://www.krem.com/article/entertainment/events/hoopfest/gonzaga-legend-adam-morrison-2024-hooptown-hall-of-fame-zags-basketball/293-5658c75b-f4dd-46da-80cd-e5d51b10f180 |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=krem.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Adam became the Gonzaga men's team's [[ball boy]].<ref name=bravehearts150/>

When he was in the eighth grade, he lost 30 pounds (14 kg),<ref name="Duel">Grant Wahl, "Jewel of a Duel", ''Sports Illustrated'', February 28, 2006. (Available online only to ''SI'' subscribers.)</ref> and while attending a basketball camp at Gonzaga during this time, he felt sick, later saying about his experience at the camp, "I think I made one shot the whole three days. I was sicker than a dog. I didn't want to play. I couldn't do anything."<ref name=bravehearts150/> Shortly after this, Morrison was diagnosed with [[diabetes mellitus type 1|type 1 diabetes]]. He took his diagnosis surprisingly well; the second time a nurse came to administer [[insulin]], he stopped her, telling her, "Since I'm going to be doing this the rest of my life, you might as well show me how to do it."<ref name=bravehearts150/> However, his illness did not keep him from becoming a star at [[Mead Senior High School]] in Spokane. In his senior year he broke single-season and career scoring records in his high school conference, and led Mead to the finals of the state tournament. Despite playing in the final game with [[hypoglycemia]] so severe that he nearly had a seizure, he scored 37 points in a losing effort. It was Mead's only loss that season. Morrison was not heavily recruited out of high school. Dave Telep of [[scout.com]] admitted, "In one of the biggest misses of my career, we left him off the Top 100 list. We ranked him the No. 26 small forward. The goal is to never make a mistake of that magnitude again".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scout Six Pack: Reappraising 2003 |url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/2/843856.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150410195805/http://scouthoops.scout.com/2/843856.html |archive-date=April 10, 2015 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |df=mdy-all}}</ref>

==College career==
Morrison arrived at [[Gonzaga University]] to play for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs]] in 2003. In his freshman year he averaged 11.4 points per game (ppg), with a season-high 22 points against [[Saint Mary's College of California|St. Mary's]]. Gonzaga won the [[West Coast Conference]] (WCC) regular-season title. Morrison was named to the WCC All-[[Freshman]] Team.<ref name="gozags">{{Cite web |title=GoZags.com Adam Morrison Bio – Gonzaga University Official Athletic Site Gonzaga University Official Athletic Site – Men's Basketball |url=http://gozags.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/morrison_adam00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090202155306/http://gozags.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/morrison_adam00.html |archive-date=February 2, 2009 |access-date=June 14, 2016}}</ref>

In his sophomore year Morrison averaged 19.0 ppg. He scored a season-high 28 points at home against [[University of San Francisco|San Francisco]], including the winning shot with 0.6 seconds remaining in the game. Gonzaga again won the WCC regular-season title. Morrison made the All-WCC First Team and was selected to the ''[[Basketball Times]]'' All-West Coast Team as well as being named an honorable mention [[Associated Press]] All-American.<ref name=gozags/>

In his junior year during Gonzaga's first two games of the 2005–06 season at the [[Maui Invitational]], Morrison played well against two of the sport's top programs. In the first round, Morrison scored 25 points in a Gonzaga win over [[University of Maryland, College Park|Maryland]]. He followed up this performance with 43 points in a triple-overtime win over [[Michigan State University|Michigan State]] in the semifinals. He matched that output against in-state rival [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] on December 4, 2005, in a losing effort. However, Morrison and the Zags bounced back a week later, defeating [[Oklahoma State University–Stillwater|Oklahoma State]] after he banked in a three-pointer with 2.5 seconds left to give Gonzaga a two-point lead and eventually the win.

In the regular season, he had 13 games of 30-plus points, with five of them over 40. At 28.1 points per game, he was the nation's leading scorer in 2005–2006. His scoring totals against teams in the "major" conferences were no less impressive; he averaged 28.5 points in 11 such games. On February 18, Morrison recorded a career high 44 points (including 37 in the second half alone) against the [[Loyola Marymount|Loyola Marymount Lions]] in a winning effort.

Morrison led the Zags with 24 points in a [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2006 NCAA tournament]] Sweet Sixteen match against [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], which the Zags lost in the final seconds after UCLA had eliminated a 17-point deficit coming out of the first half. With seconds left, the lead having slipped away after Morrison's teammates committed 3 turnovers in less than 5 seconds, Morrison broke down in tears and collapsed to the court. He was eventually helped to his feet by UCLA player [[Arron Afflalo]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 26, 2006 |title=C.W. Nevius Blog : The Big Weep—Adam Morrison cries, America squirms |work=The San Francisco Chronicle |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/blogs/sfgate/detail?blogid=18&entry_id=3790|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060412152100/http://sfgate.com/cgi-bin/blogs/sfgate/detail?blogid=18&entry_id=3790|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 12, 2006}}</ref> He has been both criticized and praised for this unbridled show of emotion. He later shared the national player of the year award with friendly rival [[JJ Redick]] of [[Duke University|Duke]]. The game against UCLA turned out to be Morrison's final collegiate game, as he later decided to turn pro, foregoing his senior year of college.

==Professional career==

===Charlotte Bobcats (2006–2009)===
Morrison was selected third overall in the [[2006 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]], behind [[Andrea Bargnani]] ([[Toronto Raptors]]) and [[LaMarcus Aldridge]] ([[Chicago Bulls]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2006 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_2006.html |access-date=2021-07-16 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On July 6, 2006, the Bobcats signed Morrison to a two-year contract. On November 1, 2006, in his NBA debut against the [[Indiana Pacers]], he scored 14 points. He was the first player drafted by [[Michael Jordan]] in his tenure as Manager of Basketball Operations with the Bobcats. He scored his career high of 30 points on December 29, 2006, in a 113–102 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]]. However, Morrison lost his starting spot midway through his rookie season, in part because of his defense and because he shot only 37% for the year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA Players – Adam Morrison |url=https://hoopshype.com/players/adam_morrison.htm |access-date=August 24, 2012 |publisher=HoopsHype}}</ref>

On October 21, 2007, the Bobcats announced that Morrison sustained a severe injury to his left knee in a preseason game against the [[L.A. Lakers]] while defending [[Luke Walton]], bending his knee laterally and falling to the ground in pain. An [[MRI]] scan performed after the game indicated a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-10-21 |title=Cats' Morrison likely out for year with knee injury |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3073563 |access-date=2021-07-16 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/morrison_tears_acl.html BOBCATS: Adam Morrison Tears ACL<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090307043745/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/morrison_tears_acl.html |date=March 7, 2009 }}</ref> On November 10, Morrison underwent surgery to repair the damage. The injury was confirmed to be a torn ACL, requiring several months of [[physical therapy]] after the knee had healed, and Morrison missed the whole 2007–08 NBA season.

===Los Angeles Lakers (2009–2010)===
On February 7, 2009, Morrison and [[Shannon Brown]] were traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for [[Vladimir Radmanović]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 7, 2009 |title=Lakers acquire adam morrison and shannon brown in exchange for vladimir radmanovic |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/090207acquiremorrisonbrown.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210121619/http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/090207acquiremorrisonbrown.html |archive-date=February 10, 2009 |access-date=February 7, 2009 |website=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref> Morrison won NBA championships with the Lakers in 2009 and 2010,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://losangeles.cbslocal.com/2016/03/25/former-laker-adam-morrison-just-gets-weirder-and-weirder-this-time-it-involves-an-apocolypse-bunker/|title = Former Laker Adam Morrison Just Gets Weirder; This Time, It Involves an Apocalypse Bunker|date = March 25, 2016}}</ref> but saw very limited playing time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/5252/adam-morrison-looking-back-looking-forward|title = Adam Morrison: Looking back, looking forward|date = August 6, 2010}}</ref> He was released following the 2009–10 season.

Following their [[2010 NBA Finals|2010 Finals]] win over the [[Boston Celtics]], several Lakers players appeared on the [[Jimmy Kimmel Live!|''Jimmy Kimmel Show'']] and clips were shown of Morrison watching on the bench or joining in the championship celebration while in street clothes. [[Kobe Bryant]] defended Morrison for his unselfishness in contributing to the team, considering him one of his favorite teammates.<ref>{{Cite web| date=February 9, 2024 |title=Phil Jackson's proudest Kobe Bryant moment: Him defending Adam Morrison on 'Jimmy Kimmel' | url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2024-02-09/kobe-bryant-phil-jackson-adam-morrison-jimmy-kimmel |access-date=April 13, 2024 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> Morrison later recalled building a relationship with Bryant that continued to the end of his career, including being thankful for the star standing up for him in the face of media criticism.<ref>{{Cite web| date=April 27, 2021 |title= Adam Morrison talks about his respect for Kobe Bryant and what made him unique as a basketball player |url=https://www.basketballnetwork.net/latest-news/adam-morrison-talks-about-his-respect-for-kobe-bryant-and-what-made-him-unique-as-a-basketball-player |website=Basketball Network |access-date=April 13, 2024}}</ref>

=== Crvena zvezda (2011) ===
Morrison signed with the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2010, but was waived at the end of training camp before playing a regular season game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2010/oct/21/wizards-cut-adam-morrison/|title = Wizards cut Adam Morrison | the Spokesman-Review}}</ref>

In September 2011, Morrison signed with [[KK Crvena zvezda]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Morrison Signs One-Year Deal With Red Star Belgrade – RealGM Wiretap |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/215561/Morrison_Signs_One_Year_Deal_With_Red_Star_Belgrade |access-date=June 14, 2016}}</ref> He was released from his contract in November 2011 to pursue other opportunities.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Amick |first=Sam |date=November 29, 2011 |title=Morrison let out of Serbian deal, may join NBA free-agent class |work=SI.com |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/sam_amick/11/29/morrison/index.html?eref=writers |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111230010718/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/sam_amick/11/29/morrison/index.html?eref=writers |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 30, 2011 |access-date=November 30, 2011}}</ref> During his 8-game stay in Belgrade (he missed one away game due to a minor injury), Morrison averaged 15.5 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 29 minutes a game, becoming his team's top scorer and the second overall top performer during the [[2011–12 ABA League|2011–12]] [[Liga ABA|Adriatic League]] season.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Morrison's Adriatic League statistics |publisher=Adriatic Basketball Association |url=http://www.adriaticbasket.info/w2/club.php?id=18 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111210063535/http://www.adriaticbasket.info/w2/club.php?id=18 |archive-date=December 10, 2011}}</ref>

=== Beşiktaş (2012) ===
In January 2012, Morrison signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Milangaz]] for the rest of the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{in lang|tr}}[http://www.ntvspor.net/haber/basketbol/56211/adam-morrison-besiktas-milangazda Adam Morrison Beşiktaş Milangaz'da]</ref> However, he left the team in April 2012 due to a lack of playing time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Morrison-Besiktas, coach Ataman conferma l'addio |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/37518/adam-morrison-and-besiktas-officially-part-ways.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525091152/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/37518/adam-morrison-and-besiktas-officially-part-ways.html |archive-date=May 25, 2012 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |df=mdy-all}}</ref>

After being absent from the NBA since being waived by the Wizards, Morrison played in the 2012 [[NBA Summer League]] for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] and averaged 5.2 points and 19.2 minutes in five games with the team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 13, 2012 |title=2012 NBA Summer League |url=http://www.nba.com/summer-league/2012/teams/nets/ |access-date=August 24, 2012 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He then joined the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]' Summer League team, averaging 20.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists on 55% FG (38–69), 61% 3-PT (13–21) and 78% FT (11–14) in 5 games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 23, 2012 |title=NBA.com: Adam Morrison's Clippers summer league stats |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/summer-league/2012/players/sl_adam_morrison/index.html}}</ref>

On September 21, 2012, Morrison signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=TRAIL BLAZERS ADD THREE PLAYERS TO TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/3421/Default.aspx |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120928060304/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/PressReleaseDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/3421/Default.aspx |archive-date=September 28, 2012 |access-date=June 14, 2016}}</ref> He was waived on October 27, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Karl, Morrison among players waived by Blazers |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/10/27/blazers-moves.ap/ |access-date=June 14, 2016}}</ref>

==National team career==
Morrison made four appearances for various junior U.S. national teams. Morrison was selected to train with the senior men's team in preparation for the 2006 [[FIBA World Championship]] but was cut prior to the tournament.<ref name="FIBA cut">{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130123013014/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/06_wcm/teamPlay/team/fe_teamPlay_teamRostNews.asp?lid_7012_newsID=14115&lid_7012_langID=1&eventID=3507&roundID=3507&langLC=en&teamNumber=379&competitionCode=&season=&playerNumber=&zone=|title="Team USA announce 15-man squad"}}, ''[[2006 FIBA World Championship|FIBA2006.com]]'', July 26, 2006. Accessed August 31, 2006.</ref>

==Coaching career==
In July 2013, Gonzaga basketball coach [[Mark Few]] announced that Morrison would become a student assistant with the basketball team. Morrison had returned to Gonzaga to take classes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 25, 2013 |title=Adam Morrison joining Gonzaga staff |url=https://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/blog/eye-on-college-basketball/22890431/adam-morrison-joining-gonzaga-staff}}</ref> After completing his undergraduate degree at Gonzaga in 2014, majoring in sports management,<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 12, 2014 |title=Gonzaga Student-Athletes Receive Undergraduate Degrees |url=https://gozags.com/news/2014/5/12/Gonzaga_Student_Athletes_Receive_Undergraduate_Degrees.aspx}}</ref> Morrison became an assistant video coordinator for the Bulldogs for the 2014–15 season, but was weighing options for his career after the season ended.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2015 |title=Gonzaga notes: Adam Morrison weighing options |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2015/jan/14/gonzaga-notes-adam-morrison-weighing-options/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 30, 2015 |title=Adam Morrison had the perfect comeback to a Duke fan's taunt about 2006 |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2015/03/adam-morrison-duke-fan}}</ref>

==Broadcasting career==
Morrison was named the color commentator for the Gonzaga men's basketball radio broadcasts with former [[KREM (TV)|KREM 2]] sports director Tom Hudson in October 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.slipperstillfits.com/2017/10/5/16431222/adam-morrison-gonzaga-bulldogs-radio-broadcast-team |title=Adam Morrison will be a new analyst for radio broadcasts this season|date=October 5, 2017 |publisher=SlipperStillFits.com|accessdate=November 25, 2022}}</ref> Since 2021 season, Morrison has hosted ''The Perimeter'' podcast, focusing on conversations with basketball and sports figures and more detailed analysis of the Gonzaga men's basketball team. The program was voted best local podcast by ''[[Inlander (newspaper)|The Inlander]]'' in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maupin |first=Will |title=Best Local Podcast: The Perimeter with Adam Morrison 2021 |url=https://www.inlander.com/best-of/2021/arts/best-local-podcast-the-perimeter-with-adam-morrison-21982546 |access-date=2024-12-15 |website=Inlander |language=en}}</ref> He also co-hosts the ''Gonzaga Nation'' podcast with former Bulldogs great [[Dan Dickau]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-23 |title=Where is Adam Morrison now? Former Gonzaga star turns to radio, podcasting after NBA career {{!}} Sporting News |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/adam-morrison-gonzaga-ncaa-nba/tojp4bexvpy9sxcjiy58fdab |access-date=2024-12-15 |website=www.sportingnews.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Morrison lives near [[Spokane, Washington|Spokane]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]], with his three children.<ref name="weitzman">Weitzman, Yaron [https://web.archive.org/web/20160807190535/http://thelab.bleacherreport.com/life-as-an-nba-draft-bust/ Life as an NBA Draft Bust: It's better than you might think. Ask Adam Morrison.] ''Bleacher Report''. June 22, 2016</ref>

===Diabetes===
Morrison was diagnosed with Type [[diabetes mellitus type 1|1 diabetes]] (insulin-dependent diabetes) at age 13. He was playing in an eighth-grade basketball game, and as the game went into overtime, he began having seizure-like symptoms, which prompted his father to take him to the hospital where the diagnosis was made. Morrison, who managed his [[diabetes]] to the point of eating exactly the same meals at the same time on game days, is considered a role model for children with the disease and their families. During his freshman year at Gonzaga, Morrison and his life with diabetes were a subject of a four-page article in ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''. On the first day that the issue appeared in retail outlets, more than 50 parents of children with diabetes contacted the Gonzaga athletic department asking if Morrison could speak to their children. Off the court, Morrison regulates his [[blood sugar]] with an [[insulin pump]] attached to his abdomen.<ref name="bravehearts150" />
